title: Special Powers Act, 1974
subtitle: Promulgated on 9 February 1974, the Act authorized preventive detention and special procedures for specified offences.
summary: Bangladesh promulgated the Special Powers Act (Act XIV of 1974) on 9 February 1974. It provided preventive measures against acts defined as prejudicial to the state and established procedures for faster trials and punishment for specified serious offences. Section 3 empowered the government to order detention to prevent a person from committing a defined “prejudicial act”; the law also provided for advisory-board review of detention orders.
heroTagline: The 1974 Act gave the government statutory powers of preventive detention.
whyItMatters: The Act placed preventive detention within Bangladesh’s post-independence legal framework. Its broad statutory definition of prejudicial acts and executive detention power made it a significant point of reference in debates about public order, executive authority and safeguards for personal liberty.

claimCitations.claim: Bangladesh promulgated the Special Powers Act (Act XIV of 1974) on 9 February 1974. It provided preventive measures against acts defined as prejudicial to the state and established procedures for faster trials and punishment for specified serious offences. Section 3 empowered the government to order detention to prevent a person from committing a defined “prejudicial act”; the law also provided for advisory-board review of detention orders.

The Act placed preventive detention within Bangladesh’s post-independence legal framework. Its broad statutory definition of prejudicial acts and executive detention power made it a significant point of reference in debates about public order, executive authority and safeguards for personal liberty.
The Act has remained a central legal reference in discussions of preventive detention and the scope of executive power in Bangladesh.
The law is part of the early republic’s institutional history and remains associated with debates over how a state balances public order with individual liberty.
